category.description: Khóa học tiếng Anh tổng quát theo khung CEFR (A1–C2)
category.name: General English

course.description: Nâng cao khả năng tiếng Anh từ A2 lên B1. Tập trung vào giao tiếp trong môi trường làm việc nhập môn, kể chuyện, diễn đạt ý kiến và viết đoạn văn ngắn.
course.title: Pre-Intermediate English

exercises.correct_answer: I write code, test applications, and attend team meetings.
exercises.explanation: Software developers primarily write code, test their work, and collaborate in meetings.
options: I write code, test applications, and attend team meetings.
I cook meals for the office every day.
I manage the company's finances and approve budgets.
I clean the office windows weekly.
exercises.question: Which of the following sentences correctly describes a typical daily task for a software developer?

exercises.explanation: Many modern workplaces have business‑casual dress codes, not formal suits daily.
exercises.question: In most offices, employees are required to wear formal suits every day.

exercises.explanation: The verb 'start' fits the infinitive form after 'usually'.
exercises.question: I usually {blank} (start) work at 9 a.m.

exercises.explanation: 'Colleague' means 'đồng nghiệp' and 'deadline' means 'hạn chót' in Vietnamese.
exercises.question: Match each workplace term with its Vietnamese meaning.

exercises.correct_answer: I work as a marketing assistant. My daily tasks include creating social media posts, analyzing campaign results, and coordinating with the design team. I also attend briefings with my manager to plan upcoming projects.
exercises.explanation: The answer translates the Vietnamese prompt and uses appropriate B1‑level vocabulary about daily work activities.
exercises.question: Write a short paragraph (3‑4 sentences) in English describing your job. Use the Vietnamese prompt: "Bạn làm việc gì và mô tả công việc hàng ngày của mình."

exercises.explanation: ‘Often’ means frequently, suitable for a regular habit.
exercises.question: Which word best completes the sentence? I ___ go to the gym after work.

exercises.explanation: ‘Commute’ refers to traveling regularly between home and workplace.
exercises.question: The verb 'to commute' means to travel to and from work.

exercises.explanation: The verb ‘drinks’ fits the routine of having coffee each morning.
exercises.question: Listen and write the missing word: She {blank} her coffee every morning before leaving.

exercises.explanation: ‘Wake up’ translates to ‘dậy’ and ‘brush teeth’ to ‘đánh răng’.
exercises.question: Match each daily activity with its Vietnamese meaning.

exercises.explanation: The natural order for this daily routine sentence is ‘I usually have breakfast at 7am’.
exercises.question: Arrange the sentence in the correct order:

exercises.correct_answer: I'm going to meet my colleague tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: 'Going to' + base verb is used for plans made before speaking.
options: I'm going to meet my colleague tomorrow.
I will meeting my colleague tomorrow.
I will to meet my colleague tomorrow.
exercises.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'going to' to express a future plan?

exercises.explanation: Present continuous is often used for scheduled personal plans.
exercises.question: The present continuous can be used to talk about a fixed arrangement in the near future.

exercises.explanation: Present continuous for a planned future event.
exercises.question: We {blank} a meeting at 3 p.m. tomorrow.

exercises.explanation: 'Will' expresses spontaneous decisions, 'going to' expresses prior plans.
exercises.question: Match each future form with its Vietnamese meaning.

exercises.correct_answer: I will visit my parents on Saturday. I'm going to watch a movie on Sunday night. We're having a barbecue on Sunday afternoon.
exercises.explanation: The answer demonstrates the three future forms: 'will' for a decision, 'going to' for a prior plan, and present continuous for a scheduled arrangement.
exercises.question: Write 2-3 sentences about your plan for the weekend using at least one 'will', one 'going to', and one present continuous form.

lessons.title: Making Plans: Will, Going To, Present Continuous

exercises.explanation: 'Could' is the past form of 'can' to talk about abilities in the past.
exercises.question: Which sentence correctly uses the past ability form?

exercises.explanation: 'Is able to' expresses present ability, and the statement is true.
exercises.question: She is able to speak three languages fluently.

exercises.explanation: 'Could' is used for ability in the past.
exercises.question: When I was a child, I {blank} ride a bike without training wheels.

exercises.correct_answer: He can do this work on weekends.
exercises.explanation: 'Có thể' in present tense translates to 'can' for ability.
options: He can do this work on weekends.
He could do this work on weekends.
He is able to do this work on weekends.
He will do this work on weekends.
exercises.question: Translate to English: 'Anh ấy có thể làm việc này vào cuối tuần.'

exercises.correct_answer: can:có thể (hiện tại), could:có thể (quá khứ)
exercises.explanation: 'Can' expresses present ability, 'could' expresses past ability.
exercises.question: Match each modal verb with its Vietnamese meaning about ability.

lessons.title: Talking About Abilities: Can, Could, Be Able To

exercises.explanation: Most offices close at 6 pm on Fridays, so this is the correct choice.
exercises.question: What time does the office usually close on Fridays?

exercises.explanation: Company policy states that a short coffee break of up to 30 minutes is permitted each morning.
exercises.question: Employees are allowed to take a 30‑minute coffee break every morning.

exercises.explanation: "Finished" correctly completes the sentence, showing the action was done before the deadline.
exercises.question: She {blank} the report before the deadline.

exercises.correct_answer: I will go to work by bicycle tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: The translation keeps the future tense (will) and the means of transport (by bicycle) correctly.
exercises.question: Translate into English: "Tôi sẽ đi làm bằng xe đạp vào ngày mai."

exercises.explanation: "Deadline" means "hạn chót" and "meeting" means "cuộc họp" in Vietnamese.
exercises.question: Match each workplace term with its Vietnamese meaning.

exercises.explanation: A sore throat refers to pain in the throat.
exercises.question: Which body part is affected when you have a sore throat?

exercises.explanation: Rash can have many causes, not only allergies.
exercises.question: If you feel a rash on your skin, it always means you have an allergic reaction.

exercises.explanation: The common symptom is chest pain.
exercises.question: I have a {blank} in my chest.

exercises.explanation: head means đầu, stomach means dạ dày.
exercises.question: Match each body part with its Vietnamese meaning.

exercises.explanation: The correct English translation of "Tôi bị đau đầu" is "I have a headache."
exercises.question: Translate the following Vietnamese sentence into English: "Tôi bị đau đầu".

exercises.explanation: ‘Throbbing’ describes a pulsating pain, which is appropriate for a headache.
exercises.question: Which phrase would you use to tell the doctor that your headache is throbbing?

exercises.explanation: 38 °C is a typical fever temperature, so the sentence is correct.
exercises.question: True or False: 'I have a fever of 38°C' is a correct way to describe a temperature.

exercises.explanation: ‘Continuously’ expresses that the coughing has been happening without stopping.
exercises.question: Complete the sentence with the appropriate word: 'I have been coughing {blank} for three days.'

exercises.correct_answer: Tôi bị đau nhói ở lưng dưới.
exercises.explanation: The translation conveys the exact meaning of the English sentence.
exercises.question: Translate the following sentence into Vietnamese: 'I have a sharp pain in my lower back.'

exercises.explanation: ‘cough’ translates to ‘ho’ and ‘fever’ translates to ‘sốt’.
exercises.question: Match each medical symptom with its Vietnamese meaning.

lessons.title: At the Doctor's: Describing Pain & Illness

exercises.explanation: Use 'should' + base verb to give advice.
options: You should to exercise every day.
exercises.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'should' to give advice about exercise?

exercises.explanation: The statement is false because you should drink at least 8 glasses of water daily.
exercises.question: You shouldn't drink at least 8 glasses of water a day.

exercises.explanation: 'Should' is used to give advice in this sentence.
exercises.question: If you want to improve your sleep, you {blank} avoid caffeine before bedtime.

exercises.correct_answer: Bạn không nên ăn quá nhiều đồ ăn nhanh.
exercises.explanation: The translation must include 'không nên' to convey 'shouldn't'.
options: Bạn không nên ăn quá nhiều đồ ăn nhanh.
Bạn không ăn quá nhiều đồ ăn nhanh.
Bạn không nên ăn đồ ăn nhanh.
Bạn không ăn đồ ăn nhanh.
exercises.question: Select the correct Vietnamese translation for the sentence: 'You shouldn't eat too much junk food.'

exercises.correct_answer: People should walk at least 30 minutes every day. They shouldn't skip breakfast because it gives energy. You should drink plenty of water. You shouldn't stay up late regularly.
exercises.explanation: The answer uses 'should' and 'shouldn't' to give clear advice about healthy habits.
exercises.question: Write 3-4 sentences about a healthy habit you think people should adopt, using 'should' or 'shouldn't'.

exercises.explanation: The Vietnamese word "bơi lội" translates to the English verb "swimming".
exercises.question: Which word means "bơi lội" in English?

exercises.explanation: Yoga focuses on flexibility and balance, not high‑intensity cardio.
exercises.question: The word "yoga" is a type of high‑intensity cardio exercise.

exercises.explanation: "Weightlifting" fits the context of a gym activity.
exercises.question: I usually go to the gym to do {blank}.

exercises.explanation: "Jog" means "chạy bộ" and "stretch" means "duỗi người".
exercises.question: Match each exercise with its Vietnamese meaning.

exercises.correct_answer: I like playing football on weekends.
exercises.explanation: The Vietnamese sentence means exactly that in English.
exercises.question: Translate the following sentence into English: "Tôi thích chơi bóng đá vào cuối tuần."

exercises.explanation: Running is an aerobic exercise that strengthens the heart.
exercises.question: Which of the following activities is most likely to improve cardiovascular health?

exercises.explanation: High sugar intake contributes to weight gain.
exercises.question: Regularly drinking sugary drinks can increase the risk of obesity.

exercises.explanation: A balanced diet means having a variety of nutrients.
exercises.question: I try to eat {blank} meals each day to stay healthy.

exercises.explanation: 'Nutrition' means dinh dưỡng in Vietnamese.
exercises.question: Translate the word 'nutrition' into Vietnamese.

exercises.correct_answer: exercise:tập thể dục, diet:chế độ ăn
exercises.explanation: Exercise = tập thể dục; diet = chế độ ăn.
exercises.question: Match each health-related term with its Vietnamese meaning.

exercises.correct_answer: I walk for thirty minutes every day to stay healthy.
exercises.explanation: Use the present simple for habits: I walk, I eat, I sleep.
exercises.question: Write one sentence about what you do to stay healthy.

exercises.explanation: "Been" is the past participle used with have/has in the present perfect.
exercises.question: Which word correctly completes the sentence: "Have you ever ___ to Japan?"

exercises.explanation: After "have" we need the past participle "eaten", not "ate".
exercises.question: The sentence "I have ate breakfast" is grammatically correct.

exercises.explanation: "Never" is used with present perfect to say something has not happened up to now.
exercises.question: She has {blank} visited London before.

exercises.explanation: "Ever" means "đã" in questions, "yet" means "vẫn" in negative sentences.
exercises.question: Match each English word with its Vietnamese meaning.

exercises.explanation: The answer uses present perfect to describe a life experience.
exercises.question: Write a short answer to the question: Have you ever tried sushi?

exercises.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time, not a duration.
options: I have been living here since five years.
I have lived here for five years.
exercises.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'since' with the present perfect?

exercises.explanation: 'For' expresses a period of time up to the present in the present perfect.
exercises.question: The present perfect can be used with 'for' to talk about a duration that started in the past and continues now.

exercises.explanation: The present perfect form of 'work' with 'since' is 'has worked'.
exercises.question: She {blank} here since March.

exercises.explanation: 'Since' = 'từ năm' (specific starting point); 'for' = 'trong vòng' (duration).
exercises.question: Match each time expression with its Vietnamese meaning.

exercises.explanation: When referring to a specific past point, use 'since' (e.g., 'since five years ago'), not 'for'.
exercises.question: Correct the sentence: 'I have known him {blank} five years ago.'

exercises.explanation: 'Bigger' is the correct comparative form of 'big'.
exercises.question: Choose the correct comparative form: My house is ___ than yours.

exercises.explanation: 'More expensive' correctly forms the comparative of 'expensive'.
exercises.question: The sentence 'This car is more expensive than the bike.' uses the correct comparative form.

exercises.explanation: 'More expensive' is the comparative used with adjectives of more than two syllables.
exercises.question: The new smartphone is {blank} than the old model.

exercises.explanation: 'Bigger' means 'to hơn' and 'more expensive' means 'đắt hơn' in Vietnamese.
exercises.question: Match each comparative adjective with its Vietnamese meaning.

exercises.correct_answer: My city is bigger than Hanoi.
exercises.explanation: The sentence correctly uses the comparative 'bigger' to compare two cities.
exercises.question: Translate into English: 'Thành phố của tôi lớn hơn Hà Nội.'

exercises.explanation: The superlative of 'big' is formed by adding -est, giving 'biggest'.
exercises.question: Which is the correct superlative form for the adjective 'big'?

exercises.explanation: It correctly uses 'most' + adjective to form a superlative.
exercises.question: The sentence 'This is the most difficult problem I have ever solved.' is a correct use of the superlative.

exercises.explanation: Superlative of 'tall' is 'the tallest'.
exercises.question: Mount Everest is {blank} mountain in the world.

exercises.correct_answer: This picture is the biggest in my collection.
exercises.explanation: Uses 'the biggest' as the superlative of 'big'.
exercises.question: Translate into English using a superlative: 'Bức tranh này là lớn nhất trong bộ sưu tập của tôi.'

exercises.explanation: Correspondence between English superlatives and Vietnamese translations.
exercises.question: Match each English superlative word with its Vietnamese meaning.

lessons.title: Superlatives: The Biggest, The Most Difficult

exercises.explanation: Present perfect is used with 'since' to talk about an action that started in the past and continues.
options: I have visited London last year.
They are going to the market yesterday.
He will finish the project tomorrow.
exercises.question: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect?

exercises.explanation: The comparative of 'good' is 'better', not 'gooder'.
exercises.question: The comparative form of 'good' is 'gooder'.

exercises.explanation: Present perfect requires 'have' + past participle.
exercises.question: I {blank} (finish) my homework already.

exercises.correct_answer: Cô ấy đã học tiếng Anh được ba năm.
exercises.explanation: Use 'được' to indicate duration with present perfect.
options: Cô ấy đã học tiếng Anh được ba năm.
Cô ấy đã học tiếng Anh trong ba năm.
Cô ấy đang học tiếng Anh ba năm.
Cô ấy sẽ học tiếng Anh ba năm.
exercises.question: Translate to Vietnamese: 'She has been studying English for three years.'

exercises.explanation: ‘bigger’ means ‘lớn hơn’, ‘smaller’ means ‘nhỏ hơn’.
exercises.question: Match each comparative adjective with its Vietnamese meaning.
